nodes.title: flow-on: make new-crate site/guide suppression attributable per crate
nodes.body:
> 🤖 SPARQ agent — out-of-scope finding from PR #5241 review round 1.

The `new-crate-site-advert` / `new-crate-guide-docs` rules now fan out per added public crate (#5241), but their `unless_paths` globs point at SHARED files (`site/src/data/surfaces.ts`, `book/src/**`). On a PR that adds two public crates and a website card / guide chapter for only ONE of them, the suppression is necessarily PR-wide, so the other crate's follow-on is lost.

`flow-on.py` already supports a `{crate}` placeholder inside `unless_paths` (resolved per crate, pinned by `MultipleNewPublicCratesTest.test_a_crate_named_artifact_suppresses_only_that_crate`); what is missing is a crate-attributable artifact path. Options: key the site rule on a per-crate `site/src/app/surface/{crate}/**` page, or check `surfaces.ts` / `book/src/SUMMARY.md` for a mention of the crate instead of matching a bare glob.

nodes.body:

nodes.title: triage-area aborts the classification pass on missing area:sparq-wrapper-gen label
nodes.body:
> 🤖 **SPARQ agent** — I am @jeswr's agent for the sparq-org/sparq RDF/SPARQL engine. @jeswr runs multiple agents; this was written by the SPARQ agent, not the PSS agent (prod-solid-server).

The scheduled area classifier aborts its entire classification pass when its generated plan includes `area:sparq-wrapper-gen`, which is absent from the repository's labels. This prevents otherwise valid rows from reaching the write loop.

Evidence: [run 34299934012, job 102304479961](https://github.com/sparq-org/sparq/actions/runs/34299934012/job/102304479961), on main `a42a9e89dec485f6a319c47cb3635c59cb5a2270`, attempt 1. The internal fixtures and independent tests passed; the live classification step then exited 2 with `ERROR: rule table produced labels that do not exist: ['area:sparq-wrapper-gen']`. The [unknown-label guard](https://github.com/sparq-org/sparq/blob/a42a9e89dec485f6a319c47cb3635c59cb5a2270/scripts/triage-area.py#L738-L746) returns before the classification/write loop, so this occurrence performed no classification or unpark writes.

A direct label lookup returned 404, and a fresh GraphQL lookup on 2026-09-09 returned null while main remained at the same commit. Exact-label and broader triage-area searches found no matching issue. Related #6335 concerns truncating enumeration at 500 labels; it does not explain this currently absent label and should remain a separate repair. The failed run does not identify the originating issue row, so the precise classification path and intended supported owner area still need to be established.

The focused repair should identify that path, use the appropriate existing supported area mapping if one is justified, and add a regression fixture for the actual input. Preserve the unknown-label fail-closed guard and prove an unsupported label still causes zero writes. Improve the diagnostic to identify the offending row/path if needed. Do not automatically create labels, guess a broad routing replacement, or replay live work as part of diagnosis.

Discovered during bounded operational triage alongside #4246; no routing change has been made.

nodes.title: No gate enforces that a newly added crates/<x>/ is registered in root [workspace].members
nodes.body:
> 🤖 SPARQ agent — discovered while correcting a decision record in `scripts/ready-issues.py::partition_path` (PR #5556 review round 1).

**What.** A PR can add `crates/<x>/Cargo.toml` without adding `crates/<x>` to the root `Cargo.toml` `[workspace].members`, and nothing blocks it:

* `scripts/gate-new-crate.py` (G1) requires a README, plus a registered benchmark and a `SKILL.md` where applicable — never workspace membership.
* `scripts/ready-issues.py::assert_workspace_tree` checks only the DECLARED → disk direction (a declared member with no directory, plus an empty tree under a glob). An extra crate directory absent from `[workspace].members` passes it.

**Why it matters.** `[workspace].members` is an explicit list with no globs, so an unregistered crate is invisible from the workspace root: it is never built, never linted, never tested, and never covered — while looking complete in the tree. Second-order effect: such a crate also has no `area:<x>` label, so `pr-area-labels.py::derive_areas` reports `unresolved` and the PR derives no labels at all (not even `area:workspace` for the manifest edit), and `_reserving_packages` then gives it nothing to reserve.

**Where.** Natural home is a new condition in `scripts/gate-new-crate.py` (it already computes the newly-added-crate set from the diff) asserting each such crate appears in root `[workspace].members`, with a hermetic `--dry-run --changed-files` fixture pinning both directions.

> 🤖 Discovered by the SPARQ worker while implementing #5128. Out-of-scope for that PR; captured as follow-up.
<!-- sparq-followup:v1 -->

nodes.title: ci-select: consider rescuing scripts/tests/test_flow_on.py too, else the #6060 flow-on carve-out is blunted in practice

In practice, though, most PRs that change the reactive rule table ALSO update `scripts/tests/test_flow_on.py` (the self-test leg `flow-on-gates.yml` runs at line ~198). `scripts/tests/test_flow_on.py` is NOT on the allowlist, so it still hits the broad `("scripts/", ...)` full-run trigger and the whole Rust matrix queues anyway — i.e. the carve-out only helps a rules-only diff.

The inertness argument looks identical (stdlib-only, no network/git, executed solely by `flow-on-gates.yml`, referenced by no Rust-CI workflow), but the allowlist currently contains NO `scripts/tests/*` entry at all and the module docstring explicitly excludes "scripts/tests/* that gate the engine". Widening it to a test file is a new class of entry and deserves its own maintainer decision + audit row rather than being smuggled in — same reasoning #6060 applied to `scripts/gate-new-crate.py`.

Wanted: a maintainer decision, and if yes the allowlist entry plus a `ChangeClassTests` row asserting a `{flow-on-rules.toml, tests/test_flow_on.py}` diff classifies `orchestration-only` with an empty affected closure.

nodes.title: Alarm on the __global__ STOCK: an active PR unattributed across more than one dispatch tick
nodes.body:
Third bullet of #4582, deliberately left out of the attribution fix (it is a monitoring mechanism, not a deriver change).

#4582 asks for an alarm on the *stock* of `__global__`, not the per-run success of the deriver: `pr-area-label` reported `success` on every run in which #4578 sat unattributed, because emitting no label IS its fail-closed contract. Per-run status structurally cannot express "an active PR has been unattributable across N consecutive dispatch ticks", which is the condition that would be a fleet-wide stall.

What this needs (none of it lives in scripts/pr-area-labels.py):
- a periodic sweep over OPEN, non-draft PRs with no `area:*` label, cross-checked against the provenance-linked source issue's areas (the `busy_packages_of_pulls` union) so an issue-rescued PR is not alarmed;
- persistence across ticks, so a PR that is unattributed once is not alarmed but one unattributed twice running is;
- an existing surface to fire on (cf. .github/workflows/ci-latency-alarm.yml / formal-alarm.yml / review-alarm.yml).

The deriver-side half of #4582 (evidence-gated `area:<crate>` provisioning for new-crate PRs) is done; this is the observability half.

nodes.title: ci-select: orchestration-only scripts/flow-on.py fires the FULL Rust CI matrix on every reactive-engine PR
nodes.body:
> 🤖 SPARQ agent — discovered while fixing CI on PR #5728 (issue #5242); out of scope for that PR.

**What.** `scripts/ci_select.py` treats any `scripts/` path as a full-run trigger (`("scripts/", "shared CI/gate/coverage script changed (executed by CI)")`), rescued only by the audited `_ORCHESTRATION_SAFE` allowlist. That allowlist already carries `scripts/triage.py`, `scripts/retriage.py`, `scripts/bd-to-issues.py`, `scripts/dispatch-plan.py`, `scripts/batch-merge.py`, `scripts/routing-validate.py`, `scripts/pr-backlog.py` — but NOT `scripts/flow-on.py` / `scripts/flow-on-rules.toml`, which are the reactive issue-minting engine and are orchestration-only by exactly the same argument (no cargo build/test/clippy/coverage/bench/fuzz/CodeQL reads them; their only CI consumers are `flow-on.yml`, `flow-on-gates.yml` and `routing-self-tests.yml`, none of which this selector gates).

**Why it matters.** A PR that changes nothing but the follow-on rules currently queues the entire Rust matrix (ci.yml, build-matrix, feature-matrix, coverage, miri/kani/asan, differential, metamorph). That is a large runner spend for a demonstrably Rust-inert diff, and it widens the flake surface of an otherwise trivial PR.

**Care needed — not a blind add.** Any new entry must satisfy the inertness obligation pinned by `OrchestrationSafeInertnessTests` in `scripts/tests/test_ci_select.py`, and `scripts/gate-new-crate.py` is deliberately NOT proposed here: it is a merge-gate script, so its rescue would need its own argument. Wanted: a maintainer decision plus the allowlist entry, the audit-test row, and the `ci/path-ownership.toml` claim if one is required.

**Explicitly NOT done in #5728.** Changing the selector during a CI-red round would have been dodging the matrix rather than fixing a defect, so it was recorded here instead.

nodes.title: sq-3ul2n.4: feat(sparq-wasm): streaming chunked ingest — StoreLoader.push(chunk)/finish(), caps peak memory, cross-chunk parser-state correctness
nodes.body:
Ingest is whole-buffer only: JS must hold the complete document (string today, bytes after sq-3ul2n.3) so peak memory is whole-doc + parsed store — the binding constraint on mobile/tab-killed browsers (research/hardware/consumer-and-targets.md tier 1-3). Add an opt-in StoreLoader binding: new StoreLoader(format) / push(chunk: Uint8Array) / finish() -> Store, feeding chunks incrementally (single-threaded, no rayon) so a ReadableStream from fetch can be piped without buffering the document. THE HARD PART is cross-chunk parser state — Turtle prefixes, blank-node scopes, string literals and multi-byte UTF-8 sequences split across chunk boundaries (see the rust-parallel-parsing skill's chunk-boundary hazards; the serial wasm path uses nt::parse_chunk for N-Triples and oxttl for Turtle/TriG — prefer oxttl's incremental/low-level API and a carry-buffer for nt, do NOT invent a new parser). If sparq-core API changes are unavoidable, STOP and escalate (needs_architect) rather than widening the surface silently. OPT-IN feature 'stream-ingest', OFF by default, lean bundle byte-identical. NON-PARALLEL: same-crate chain, dep on sq-3ul2n.3. | FILES: crates/sparq-wasm/src/stream.rs (new), crates/sparq-wasm/src/lib.rs (mod line), crates/sparq-wasm/Cargo.toml (feature), crates/sparq-wasm/tests/web.rs (tests). | INVARIANT: result-equivalence — for ANY chunking of the same document (including splits inside tokens, literals, and multi-byte UTF-8) the finished store equals the whole-buffer load; fail-closed with the same error surface on malformed input; peak wasm-side buffering is O(chunk + carry), never O(document); lean default bundle byte-identical feature-OFF. | ACCEPTANCE: cd crates/sparq-wasm && wasm-pack test --node -- --features stream-ingest passes a seeded randomized chunk-split property test (Turtle fixture with prefixes + bnodes + multi-byte chars + long literals; >=50 random splits) asserting chunked==whole, plus malformed-input parity tests; no-features test run still green; wasm_bundle_bytes gate unchanged.

<!-- bd-id:sq-3ul2n.4 -->
Parent: #2580

nodes.title: sq-3ul2n.6: spike(sparq-wasm): allocator + linear-memory tuning — dlmalloc vs talc, initial-memory/stack-size, adopt only on measured win
nodes.body:
The wasm build runs rustc's default dlmalloc with zero linear-memory tuning (no initial-memory/max-memory/stack-size link args anywhere — verified). Parse+dictionary build is allocation-heavy and single-threaded, so allocator overhead lands squarely on the ingest path. SPIKE: (1) add an OPT-IN 'alloc-talc' feature installing talc (or lol_alloc if talc regresses) as #[global_allocator] in a new src/alloc.rs; (2) experiment with sizing initial memory to skip early memory.grow steps during typical ingest; (3) measure BOTH feature states with the existing advisory scripts (crates/sparq-wasm/test/perf.cjs + mem.cjs — load throughput, bytes/triple, query latencies) and record the verdict as a bd note + PR-body table labelled ADVISORY/NON-CANONICAL. ADOPT (flip the shipped js build to enable it) only if the measured win is consistent and non-trivial AND the bundle-size cost fits the wasm_bundle_bytes discipline; otherwise close the spike with the negative verdict recorded (negative results are results — cf bench/SPIKES.md culture). nodes.title: [dedup] brTPF position=term wire grammar duplicated across server parser and fedclient encoder with no shared code and no cross-crate round-trip test; give the codec one home
nodes.body:
> 🤖 SPARQ agent

Part of the maintainability program (see umbrella issue; multi-agent survey + independent verification, 2026-07-22).

## Evidence
Server side: /home/ubuntu/sparq/crates/sparq-server/src/tpf.rs parse_bindings / parse_bindings_capped (lines 389/416) parse the line-oriented `position=term` text wire (N-Triples-decorated terms). Client side: /home/ubuntu/sparq/crates/sparq-fedclient/src/wire.rs (709 LOC) encode_bindings_text (line 399) writes the same grammar; its module doc's load-bearing claim is that 'the text form matches the server's parser grammar (the same position=term grammar the server's parse_bindings reads)' — a cross-crate wire contract kept in sync only by tests (fedclient dev-depends on sparq-server for round-trips).

## Proposal
Move the brTPF binding-wire codec — the text grammar (parse + encode of the line-oriented position=term / N-Triples-term form) and wire.rs's binary form — into one shared home so the two ends cannot desynchronize. Home options: (a) a feature-gated module in sparq-fedplan (fedclient already depends on it; sparq-server's opt-in brtpf feature adds an opt-in server→fedplan edge — no cycle, fedplan has zero workspace deps; slight scope stretch vs fedplan's descriptor-only charter), or (b) a tiny new crate (e.g. sparq-brtpf-wire). Either way the shared home needs a shared binding/term model (today server uses its own Binding/parse_term while fedclient uses FragBinding/FragTerm), with thin adapters on each side. Correction to the original evidence: there is currently NO cross-crate round-trip test at all — fedclient's sparq-server dev-dep does not enable brtpf and is used only for the endpoint loopback test — so as an interim step (or acceptance test for the consolidation), add a round-trip test that feeds encode_bindings_text output through the server's parse_bindings_capped.

## Acceptance
- The proposal above is implemented (or, for upstream items, a minimal-diff draft PR is opened upstream in repo style and @jeswr tagged first per the upstream protocol).
- No behavior change: existing tests/gates stay green in both feature states; byte-conventions changes (if any) update their exact-match tests as named above.
- Duplicated sites are deleted, not deprecated; a mutation tripwire or test guards against re-divergence where the proposal names one.

_Effort: small · Category: duplication_

nodes.title: [new-lib] Extract sparq-vectors::diskann (persistent Vamana/DiskANN + .spqg format + PQ re-rank layer) into a stand-alone pure-Rust crates.io crate
nodes.body:
> 🤖 SPARQ agent

Part of the maintainability program (see umbrella issue; multi-agent survey + independent verification, 2026-07-22).

## Evidence
/home/ubuntu/sparq/crates/sparq-vectors/src/diskann.rs (1285 LOC): a self-contained Vamana implementation — RobustPrune with the two-pass alpha schedule, greedy beam search, and a versioned, mmap-friendly .spqg on-disk format — written precisely because instant-distance's HNSW is a closed graph that cannot be persisted (module docs). The Rust ecosystem has no maintained pure-Rust persistent-ANN/DiskANN crate. Coupling to sparq is thin: it reads vectors from the crate's VectorStore and embeds a graph fingerprint (fingerprint.rs) for staleness rejection — both injectable behind a small vector-source trait.

## Proposal
Extract build + search + the versioned .spqg on-disk format from crates/sparq-vectors/src/diskann.rs into a new crates.io crate behind a small VectorSource trait. Scope must also include: (a) the crate::quant PQ layer (ProductQuantizer/EncodedStore/DistanceTable) since DiskANN's search-on-PQ/re-rank-on-mmap path depends on it and it is only VectorStore+Id coupled; (b) the shared mmap/wasm read-backing abstraction (open_backing/Bytes in store.rs) that .spqg reads go through. Genericize the 24-byte header fingerprint as an opaque staleness token supplied by the consumer; sparq-vectors keeps dict-id/Term keying and Fingerprint::of(Graph) computation as consumer glue. The recall/throughput harnesses (examples/pareto_bench.rs, tests/diskann.rs, staleness_contract.rs, recall.rs) move with it as the crate's bench/test suite. Fills a real ecosystem gap: no maintained pure-Rust persistent-ANN/DiskANN crate exists (instant-distance is closed-graph HNSW; hnsw_rs was rejected in this repo's own Cargo.toml comments for dependency-tree weight; usearch is a C++ binding).

## Acceptance
- The proposal above is implemented (or, for upstream items, a minimal-diff draft PR is opened upstream in repo style and @jeswr tagged first per the upstream protocol).
- No behavior change: existing tests/gates stay green in both feature states; byte-conventions changes (if any) update their exact-match tests as named above.

nodes.title: sq-7d3dj.34.2.3: Streaming pipeline v1 (M1, seed-lex order contract §5.1): classifier + block driver over the emit sink — first solutions before the join completes
nodes.body:
Design record research/lazy-pull-incremental-emission.md §5 + §5.1 AS AMENDED by decision sq-7d3dj.34.2.7 (PR #2180) — the original byte-identity-for-bind-chains contract is RETIRED; read §5.1 (seed-lex order contract) + §8.1/§8.2 as amended before implementing.

NEW module crates/sparq-engine/src/stream_pipeline.rs + ONE hook in exec::eval_select_json_emit (after single_pattern_scan_json_emit, before the buffered path) + mod line in lib.rs + rustdoc amendment on query_json_stream_with_budget / query_json_stream_prepared_with_budget (two-mode order contract: byte-identical where structural, deterministic-relaxed for admitted join chains).

DRIVER MODEL (decided, §5.1): block-slice the seed with the adaptive ramp (STREAM_BLOCK_FIRST ~4096 doubling to STREAM_BLOCK_MAX ~65536; constants OVERRIDABLE via the stream_pipeline_testing toggle so tests can force tiny blocks) and run each block through the bind_join chain. EMISSION ORDER IS SEED-LEX ORDER: within a block, use an FxHashMap grouping ONLY as a scan cache (one index scan per distinct join value, matches cached), then walk the block's rows IN ORDER appending each row's matches contiguously in match-scan order. Do NOT replicate the buffered kernel's hash-bucket group-loop order (exec.rs:8058-8100; counterexample in sq-7d3dj.34.2.7). Order composes through the chain as lexicographic (seed row, match1, match2, ...).

First-seen hash DISTINCT persists across blocks and emits survivors immediately; LIMIT early-exits the driver; JSON head emitted before the seed scan; budget::check per block; ControlFlow::Break aborts.

HARNESS EXTENSION (tests/stream_pipeline_equivalence.rs — keep the existing byte-diff suite for fallback/buffered shapes, ADD the §5.1 suites): (a) DISTINCT shapes → solution-SET equality vs buffered + head + valid JSON; (b) non-slice non-distinct → solution-MULTISET equality; (c) Slice → streamed solutions are a sub-multiset of the UN-sliced buffered result with the buffered sliced count; (d) determinism → streamed path run twice is byte-identical to itself; (e) fallback shapes → byte-identical + testing-stats assertion of the path taken. MULTI-BLOCK NON-VACUITY IS MANDATORY — the current 4000-row corpus fits one default block and masked the .2.7 bug.

nodes.title: sq-rsd3v.1: Single-use nullifier primitive (in-circuit Poseidon2(hsk, epoch)) — the one genuinely-absent ZK gadget
nodes.body:
The ONE genuinely-absent primitive in the estate (grep across sparq-zk + sparq-zk-compose finds no nullifier/double-spend). Prerequisite for unlinkable presentation (sq-wvne) AND delegation non-replayability (sq-l5og).

NOT a 'generalised audit-#4 store'. The shipped audit-#4 nonce binding is purely verifier-side (every circuit does `let _ = challenge;`; binding = public-input field-0 byte-compare). The nullifier is NEW in-circuit soundness surface:
(a) nf = Poseidon2([ZKSIG_NF, hsk, epoch]) computed IN-CIRCUIT from the WITNESSED hsk, asserted equal to public nf (new ZKSIG_NF domain tag in crates/sparq-zk/src/sig.rs).
(b) soundness rides BOTH the holder-PoK DL-binding of hsk (NOT-yet-sound, sq-qhy4) AND Poseidon2 domain-separated collision-resistance over (ZKSIG_NF, hsk, epoch).
(c) GRANULARITY claimed = per-holder-per-epoch rate-limit (nf binds hsk+epoch but NOT the credential/commitment, so one key across distinct credentials in one epoch COLLIDES). It is NOT a per-presentation single-use token; a per-presentation variant folds the commitment in and is a SEPARATE larger obligation.
(d) double-spend enforcement = verifier-side seen-set of nf per epoch, fail-closed on collision.

DELIVER: zk-nullifier opt-in feature; the new in-circuit gadget + ZKSIG_NF tag + verifier seen-set gate; forge-and-verify regression test (replay same nf in same epoch must fail-closed). Honest scope notes per research/zk-inference-and-credentials.md §6.3. NOT-yet-sound (sq-qhy4). [OPUS-4.8]

nodes.title: Papers track: access-controlled-query BENCHMARK (WAC + ACP + ODRL) over use-case-representative datasets + sparq evaluation (maintainer directive 2026-07-06)
nodes.body:
> 🤖 **SPARQ agent** — recording a maintainer directive (in-session, 2026-07-06) verbatim.

## Maintainer directive

> In the papers track; could you make one of the papers a benchmark for access controlled queries (which can benchmark WAC, ACP and ODRL by having benchmarks for each) on datasets that effectively represent diffferent use cases (e.g. personal data storage, commcial rpoject management like graph metrix, financial serices usage, other ...) and an evauation of sparq against that benchmark.

## Program shape (design-first)

A Fable architect decomposes into: benchmark methodology design record → dataset generators (parameterized, per use case: personal data storage / commercial project management / financial services / +1 more) → ACL-shape + query workloads per model (WAC, ACP, ODRL — spec-level, implementation-agnostic) → correctness oracles (a benchmark passable by an unsound implementation is useless) → harness (registered in the run-all-benchmarks catalog, sq-hz0g2) → sparq evaluation → the paper.

Constraints and estate ties:
- **Honesty:** canonical wall-clock per the EC2 protocol (quota still gated, #1364) — deterministic metrics + work-box provisional ratios until then; the paper stays draft until canonical runs; no perf numbers in markdown outside bench/.
- **Reconcile with the papers program:** the odrl-policy-bridge paper's pending decision-agreement study (vs ODRE/OAC) and the sq-3ovwp fold-or-kill decision on solid-acl-conformance — this benchmark may be the natural vehicle/home for both.
- **Estate:** sparq-solid WAC/ACP/ODRL (+ the #1582 ODRL-as-N3 program may change internals — benchmark at the spec surface), the PSS beyond-50k concurrency track (#1604), decision/query_as/invalidation hot paths (#1577/#1584/#1585/#1569).

Refs: sq-gum8, sq-3ovwp, sq-hz0g2, #1604, #1582.
